gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: He was exhausted because he had ___ the cooking for twenty people.
gaps.explanation: do the cooking is the fixed phrase; after 'had' the past participle 'done' is needed.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ a loud argument in the garden last night.
gaps.explanation: have an argument (with somebody) is the fixed collocation for quarrelling.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: Could you ___ me a favour and close the window?
gaps.explanation: do somebody a favour is the fixed collocation; 'make a favour' is a common error.
